title: Private VPC: Network upgrade rollback safety, offline bootstrap constraints, and telemetry redaction PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers operating Redwood Private in fully isolated VPCs or air-gapped sites require deterministic upgrade behavior, predictable rollback safety, and guarantees that bootstrap and health telemetry do not leak sensitive metadata. This PRD defines the requirements and acceptance criteria for: (1) network-aware upgrade and rollback playbooks, (2) offline/bootstrap validation and staged image validation for air-gapped installs, and (3) telemetry redaction and minimal outbound handshake during initial operator or agent bootstrap. Goal: ship a set of platform controls and operator checks that allow upgrades to be safely staged, automatically halted or rolled back on network regressions, and to ensure telemetry emitted during bootstrap is scrubbed and optional for air-gapped customers.
scope: In-scope: upgrade staging flow that verifies network path viability before advancing to each control-plane stage
In-scope: automated rollback triggers based on deterministic network/health checks and canary metric deltas
In-scope: offline bootstrap validation harness for customers with no outbound connectivity (image signing, manifest checksums, KMS policy validation steps)
In-scope: telemetry redaction options and a zero-outbound-mode for first-boot probes; local operator logs retained for customer ops
In-scope: operator CLI flags and Console controls to assert 'no-telemetry' and 'defer-upgrade' modes
out_of_scope: Out-of-scope: full redesign of the operator — this PRD augments existing operator flows with checks rather than replacing them
Out-of-scope: changes to public Hosted API behavior or non-private Dedicated clusters
Out-of-scope: long-term multi-site replication protocols (addressed in a follow-up project)
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade safety gate: when performing a control-plane upgrade, each stage must run a Network Reachability Check (NR-check) that verifies expected internal endpoints and any configured external proxies (if configured) within a 30s timeout; failure causes stage to mark 'blocked' and surface automated rollback instructions

Rollback triggers: any of the following occurring during or within 15 minutes post-stage should auto-mark a canary as failed and initiate the rollback playbook: increased 99th latency >50% vs baseline, persistent packet loss >2% to core services, control-plane pod restarts >3 in 5 minutes

Offline bootstrap: the operator must be able to validate a local image bundle and manifest purely from local artifacts and KMS-provided keys without requiring any outbound egress; validation must include signed manifest, checksum verification, and a staged-file integrity check

Telemetry redaction: by default, bootstrap probes must not include customer identifiers (account IDs, VPC subnet CIDRs, or node IPs). A 'telemetry-level' operator flag must allow customers to choose: none | minimal (anonymized metrics) | full (opt-in). Default for private installs is 'minimal'.

Zero-outbound mode: with 'no-telemetry' enabled, the bootstrap sequence must complete without any outbound TCP connections; operator must fail with a clear actionable error if required images or keys are absent locally

Operatorless-onboarding validation: a hashed-compatibility file generated at build time must be validated during bootstrap; mismatch must block install and produce a downloadable validation bundle for customer support

Canary metric thresholds: console canary dashboard must surface canary pass/fail and store windowed aggregates for 30 days in private deployments (or local retention policy), and the canary pass/fail must be an explicit blocking signal for rollouts
Documentation: customer-facing runbook and in-console guidance for 'staged rollback' and 'force rollback' actions must be present before GA
rollback_playbook: Step 0: Mark the upgrade as Suspended in Console and prevent new traffic from routing to updated nodes
Step 1: Revert control-plane image tags to previous stable manifest from local cache or mirrored repository
Step 2: Invoke operator roll-forward safety check to ensure previous replica count and KV cache state are restored
Step 3: If rollback fails to restore health within 10 minutes, escalate to manual intervention and collect 'pre-rollback' and 'post-rollback' tarball (automated collection endpoint will be available)
Step 4: Notify customer via configured Slack/Email hooks and annotate incident in cluster audit logs
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Alpha): implement checks in a feature-flagged operator path and expose 'telemetry-level' flag; test in internal private clusters
Phase 1 (Beta): release to 3 pilot customers with mixed connectivity profiles (fully air-gapped, limited egress, minimal egress) and collect telemetry opt-in stats
Phase 2 (GA): enable default 'minimal' telemetry for all new private installs; provide a migration CLI that applies the new operator flag and validates local mirror artifacts
Backwards compatibility: operator will accept both old and new manifests; upgrade flow will perform a preflight that warns customers when their mirrored repositories or bundle artifacts are missing
test_plan: Automated CI: inject synthetic network failures (packet loss, DNS failure, proxy auth failure) during staged upgrades and assert rollback triggers
Airgap e2e: run air-gapped installation in isolated CI farm that simulates zero-outbound and validate operator completes local bundle verification
Redaction verification: fuzz tests that ensure PII and metadata fields are absent from telemetry payloads in 'no-telemetry' and 'minimal' modes
Load canary: run traffic simulation to measure baseline latency and exercise canary thresholds for 30, 60, 120 minute windows
Manual runbooks: QA engineer-run checklist for staged rollback and post-rollback recovery within a controlled test cluster
dependencies: ENG-19862 (operator: staged upgrade hooks and health probes)
ENG-20211 (mirror: signed-bundle validation and manifest checksum tooling)
ENG-21450 (console: canary dashboard and 'suspend rollout' control)
SEC-313 (telemetry schema review and PII redaction rules)
Docs-44 (customer runbooks and onboarding guide updates)
notes: Trade-offs: strong default redaction reduces out-of-the-box observability for our SREs — mitigated via an opt-in debug flag and downloadable debug bundles
Decision: prefer deterministic local validation over requiring a central 'bootstrap service' to support air-gapped customers
Open question: whether to allow configurable network probes to 3rd-party egress proxies vs restricting to internal endpoint-only checks
Monitoring: for 'minimal' telemetry we will emit aggregated counters (success/fail counts) without IPs or account identifiers; still requires SEC sign-off
